en.title: Emmy Awards 2026: Crime Dramas Dominate as Mariska Hargitay Hosts
en.summary: The 2026 Emmy Awards saw a strong showing from crime-centric programming, highlighted by the hosting duties of Mariska Hargitay and numerous nominations in the genre. From gripping dramas to witty comedies, the night celebrated the enduring appeal of storytelling that delves into the darker corners of human nature.
en.body:
The Television Academy's annual celebration of broadcast excellence, the 2026 Emmy Awards, felt distinctly steeped in the world of crime this year. Hosting the prestigious event was none other than **Mariska Hargitay**, a familiar face to millions as Detective Olivia Benson on the long-running **Law & Order: SVU**. Hargitay’s opening segment itself paid homage to the crime genre, setting a tone that resonated throughout the night's nominations and wins. The presence of crime-related narratives was undeniable, spanning across the most competitive categories.

In the race for Outstanding Drama Series, titles like **Slow Horses** and **The Diplomat** showcased the genre's breadth, while the Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series category saw intense competition with nominees like **Beef** and **The Beast In Me**. Even the comedy sphere wasn't entirely immune, with **Only Murders in the Building**, a show built on a murder mystery premise, securing a nomination. This pervasive influence underscores the genre's robust health and its ability to engage viewers with compelling mysteries and character-driven stories.

## A Night of Crime and Celebration

The Emmys 2026 recognized a diverse array of talent and storytelling. While specific winners in every category are being updated live, the nominations themselves painted a clear picture of the genre's dominance. The selection of **Mariska Hargitay** as host was a deliberate nod to the enduring power of crime television. Her twenty-seven-year tenure as Olivia Benson has made her an icon, and her opening tribute to the character and show solidified the evening's thematic leanings. The awards ceremony, as always, provided a platform to celebrate the craft behind these captivating narratives, from intricate plotting to nuanced character development.

## What the Wins Mean for Fans

For fans of crime fiction and television, the 2026 Emmys offered a moment of validation. The sheer volume of crime-related programming recognized by the Academy signals a continued appetite for these stories, not just in television but across all forms of media. The success of shows like **The Pitt**, which took home the award for Outstanding Drama Series, and the broad appeal of nominated comedies like **Only Murders in the Building**, demonstrate that audiences are drawn to narratives that explore suspense, mystery, and the complexities of justice. This widespread recognition ensures that creators will continue to be inspired to push the boundaries of the genre, promising even more compelling crime content in the years to come.

## What's Next

As the dust settles on the 2026 Emmy Awards, attention will undoubtedly turn to upcoming projects in the crime genre. With **Rob Reiner** receiving a posthumous Emmy for his work on **The Bear**, and **Vince Gilligan** also a notable winner, the creative forces behind these acclaimed shows are sure to be developing new projects. Fans can anticipate further announcements regarding future seasons and new ventures from these celebrated storytellers.

content_raw: Featured image credit: NBC via Variety As long as we’ve had TV, we’ve had crime shows. Technically speaking, we even had “crime shows” before that: radio programs, film series, and of course serialized stories and novels. And for seventy-eight years, the Television Academy has reflected this investment in its annual Emmy Awards. This year, though, it felt to me like the crime genres were really present at the Emmys… not simply in the programs nominated, but also in the choice of host: Mariska Hargitay, one of the most familiar faces in all of crime TV. For twenty-seven years, she has played Detective Olivia Benson on Law and Order: SVU . And her cold open was an homage to that show and character, doubling down on the crimey vibes reflected in the nominees.
